title: Does RAG + Deterministic Verification Reduce Critical Intent→Configuration Errors? A Preregistered Paired Study (200 tasks)
abstract: We study whether a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline combined with a deterministic network-configuration verifier and a single automated repair iteration ("guarded") reduces critical configuration errors relative to LLM-only generation ("baseline") for intent→configuration tasks. We preregistered a paired design over 200 natural-language intents (study-2026-netops-rag-verifier-001) and executed the frozen plan using gpt-5-mini and a containerized Batfish-style verifier. Confirmatory result: baseline produced 199/200 sandbox-successful configurations and guarded produced 200/200 (absolute paired improvement = 0.005; McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI 0.00–0.015). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥30% relative reduction in critical-error rate) is not supported. We report the completed preregistration, execution manifest, scored episodes, and deterministic audit artifacts. Key limitations: single hosted LLM, sandboxed verifier environment, limited task bank (200 tasks), and unavoidable uncertainty about closed-source model training-data overlap.

sections.introduction: Problem. Intent-driven NetOps requires translating operator intent into correct low-level configurations; LLMs are promising but prone to unsafe outputs. Research question (preregistered): Does RAG+deterministic verifier+one automated repair iteration reduce paired critical configuration errors by ≥30% relative to LLM-only across a 200-task paired corpus? Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired experiment (study-2026-netops-rag-verifier-001). (2) A reproducible execution manifest and scoring archive (200 paired episodes, gpt-5-mini, containerized verifier). (3) Confirmatory outcome and failure analysis; full disclosure of methods, prompts, tools, and hashes.
sections.related_work: Positioning. Prior NetOps and intent→configuration work motivates guarded generate–validate–repair pipelines and use of deterministic verifiers (e.g., NetConfEval, intent→config studies). We relied on recent surveys and verification tools to shape the design and metrics (see cited references). We preregistered against benchmarks and RAG/verifier literature to avoid post-hoc specification.
sections.methodology: Preregistration summary (frozen before execution). Study ID: study-2026-netops-rag-verifier-001. Design: paired within-task comparison, N=200 intents balanced across topology/protocol families (preregistration snapshot). Intervention: guarded pipeline = RAG grounding + gpt-5-mini generation + deterministic configuration verifier (Batfish-style) + single automated repair pass when verifier flags a problem. Baseline: LLM-only (same base model and primary prompt, no retrieval or verifier loop). Primary estimand: paired difference in per-task critical-error probability. Primary test: McNemar exact two-sided (α=0.05). Execution artifacts and raw outputs, model-call traces, and hashes recorded in the execution manifest.
sections.results: Confirmatory (pre-specified). Complete paired count = 200 tasks. Baseline pipeline: 199 successful (sandbox-verifier pass) / 200. Guarded pipeline: 200/200 successful. Aggregate paired contingency: n11 (both success) = 199; n10 (baseline success, guarded failure) = 0; n01 (baseline failure, guarded success) = 1; n00 (both fail) = 0. Absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. 95% bootstrap percentile CI for absolute paired difference: [0.00, 0.015] (bootstrap_seed=1729, 10k resamples). Interpretation: the large, pre-specified ≥30% relative reduction target was not reached; the observed effect is a 0.5 percentage-point absolute improvement with wide practical uncertainty around near-zero effect. Secondary analyses (latency, detailed subgroup hypothesis tests) were pre-specified but no confirmatory secondary result is reported in the primary analysis artifact set.
sections.discussion: Confirmatory interpretation. Both pipelines produced near-perfect sandbox outcomes; RAG+verifier produced one additional guarded success relative to baseline (absolute 0.5%). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥30% relative reduction) is not supported by these data. Possible mechanistic reasons: (a) the chosen LLM (gpt-5-mini) already performs strongly for the selected 200 tasks; (b) the sandbox verification target set may omit real-world failure modes; (c) retrieval-corpus overlap or narrow task construction can reduce observed headroom for improvement. Exploratory analyses (planned in preregistration) remain available in the archived artifacts for future work. Operational implication: in this controlled sandbox, the added guarded machinery produced only a marginal absolute gain over a high-performing LLM; deployments should weigh verifier cost/latency against marginal reliability improvements.
sections.conclusion: We report a complete preregistered paired experiment comparing RAG+deterministic verification+one automated repair vs LLM-only on 200 intent→configuration tasks using gpt-5-mini. The preregistered primary hypothesis was not supported: observed absolute improvement was 0.5% (McNemar p=1.0; 95% CI 0.0–0.015). All preregistered artifacts, prompts, raw outputs, verifier traces, and hashes are archived in the execution manifest. We emphasize the study's narrow scope (sandbox, single model) and present the artifacts to facilitate replication and more extensive follow-ups that vary model class, retrieval corpora, verifier strength, and real-world deployment conditions.

limitations: Single-model scope: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not generalize to other LLM families or larger/smaller variants.
Sandbox evaluation: correctness was measured against a containerized deterministic verifier (Batfish-style) and synthetic/sandboxed network simulations; production deployment outcomes may differ.
Limited task bank: N=200 intents (preregistered) provides paired power for medium effects but limited generality across all NetOps scenarios.

Possible training-data overlap: closed-source model training data overlap with retrieval/test materials cannot be fully ruled out; we applied deterministic leakage detectors and report sensitivity artifacts but residual uncertainty remains.
Null/near-null headroom: baseline LLM performance was near-perfect in this task set, leaving little headroom for large relative gains from the guarded pipeline.

Latency/cost trade-offs: preregistered latency analyses were planned but are not reported as confirmatory in the primary analysis artifact set; practical operator-tolerance and cost-benefit require further evaluation.

External validity: multi-vendor devices, live traffic dynamics, operator workflows, and adversarial/environmental conditions were not evaluated; results should not be interpreted as production-readiness evidence.
